description.value: The study examined alterations in resting-state regional brain activity and seed-based functional connectivity in patients with congenital unilateral conductive hearing loss compared with normal-hearing controls, and assessed associations with clinical features and the effect of global signal regression.

design.value: A cross-sectional case-control resting-state fMRI study compared patients with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia with age- and sex-matched normal hearing controls; ALFF, fALFF, ReHo and SBFC were analyzed with and without global signal regression.

spans.text: The present study included 27 patients aged 11–40 years with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia (UM group) and 27 age- and sex-matched normal hearing individuals aged 11–35 years (NC group).
